info.title: Homebase read door
info.summary: Read-only questions about one household's money and health, answered by the app's own maths.
info.description:
This is the reading half of a private household app. It answers questions. It changes nothing.

Six things to know before you use it:

1. Every number here is computed by the same code the household's own screens use. Do not re-derive, re-total, or estimate anything you are given. If a figure is not in a reply, say it is not available rather than working it out.
2. There is one clock, and it is Arizona (no daylight saving). The door builds that clock once per request. Do not send your own dates except where a tool asks for them.
3. No individual charges, no merchant names, no bank descriptors, and no account numbers ever come out of this door. Category totals only. If someone asks which charge, the answer is to open the app.
4. Names that do come out (a bill, a debt, an account, a budget line) are typed by the household and are shortened and cleaned on the way out. Say them as given. Never repeat one outside the conversation.
5. Say which half is measured. The numbers are measured. Anything you add around them is your judgement, and you must label it as yours.
6. Every call is written to an audit log the household can read.

There is no write endpoint in this door and no search endpoint. Those are not switched off; they do not exist here.

get.description: Returns this document. It needs the same token as every other call, so a stranger cannot read the list of tools.

post.summary: Does the app disagree with itself?
post.description:
Runs the household's own self-checks. Each check asks one question in plain words and comes back ok or fail.

Use it when asked whether anything is wrong, whether the books add up, or before quoting a lot of figures at once. If a check fails, report the check's own words and say the app is the place to see which row it is about. Do not guess at the cause, and do not offer an opinion beside a check's verdict.

The number of checks can change as the app grows. Read the ids you are given; do not assume a fixed list.

200.description: Every check, in the order the app runs them.

oneFailure.summary: Seven checks, one of them failing. Invented figures.

checks.question: Do your bills add up the same way on every screen?
checks.detail: All 14 fixed bills are counted identically by the budget and the calendar.

checks.question: Does each budget line equal the charges behind it?
checks.detail: Every budget line equals the sum of the charges it shows.

checks.question: Could money vanish into a category nothing watches?
checks.detail: All 11 spending categories in use are either budgeted or deliberately set outside the budget.

checks.question: Do the budget lines add up to the budget?
checks.detail: The lines total $1,500.00, matching the envelope.

checks.question: Do split charges still add up to what you paid?
checks.detail: 1 split charge does not add up to what was paid. Open the app to see which one.

checks.question: Is every bill marked paid actually paid in full?
checks.detail: All 6 settled fixed-bill cycles from this month on were paid in full.

checks.question: Is any bill recorded as paid twice?
checks.detail: Every settled bill cycle is claimed by exactly one charge.

post.summary: How much cash is there right now?
post.description:
Cash across the accounts that hold money. Credit cards are left out on purpose: a card is a debt, not cash, and it belongs to finance.debts.

`available` is the figure the bank calls available, and it is ALREADY reduced by anything still processing. `pending_hold` is shown beside it so a person can see how much of that reduction is recent. Never add the two together, and never call `available` a posted balance.

Use it for "what can I spend", "how much is in the account", "are we okay until payday". For what is left of a budget line this cycle, use finance.budget_status instead.

200.description: The cash total, the hold beside it, and one entry per cash account.

post.summary: What is owed, in the order it is being attacked?
post.description:
The debts in the household's chosen payoff order, with balances.

There is no payoff date and no debt-free month in this reply, and you must not calculate one. The app has that maths, this door does not expose it yet, and an invented date is exactly the kind of confident wrong number this system exists to stop.

`total` is present only when the door can get it from the app's own plan maths. If it is missing, say the individual balances and stop; do not add them up yourself.

post.summary: Where did the money go between two dates?
post.description:
Totals by category over an inclusive date range. Both dates are required and both are plain calendar dates, YYYY-MM-DD.

You choose the window, so choose it out loud: say which dates you asked about before you say the numbers. If the person said "this month" or "last week", state the exact dates you used, because the door will not guess for you.

Charges that are still processing are counted, on purpose, because the cash figure in finance.position has already been reduced by them.

This is the only spending tool there is. There is no way to list charges, and no way to ask about one merchant. If that is what is wanted, say the app is the place for it.

200.description: One total per category that had spending in the window. A category with nothing spent may be absent.

post.summary: What is left in the budget this pay cycle?
post.description:
The budget for the pay cycle that contains right now, line by line.

A pay cycle is not a month. It runs from the last payday through the day before the next one, so it crosses the end of the month, and the targets here are one cycle's share of a monthly figure — not the monthly figure itself. Say "this pay cycle" when you report these numbers, and give the cycle's dates if there is any chance of confusion.

`left` can be negative. Report it as over by that amount rather than dressing it up.

200.description: The cycle window, the envelope, and each line.

post.summary: Which way is the weight going?
post.description:
One person's latest weigh-in, this week's running average, and the trend in pounds per week.

The trend is a least-squares slope over every entry on file, so it is steadier than the difference between two mornings. Negative means losing. It is `null` when there are fewer than two entries — in that case say there is not enough logged yet, and do not say zero.

`week_count` is how many days this week have a weigh-in. A one-day average is not a week; say so.

notEnoughYet.summary: One entry on file, so there is no trend.

bearerAuth.description: The token in `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. One token per person. It is held by the caller and never appears in a reply.

museToken.name: X-Muse-Token
museToken.description: The same token in a plain header, for a caller that cannot set Authorization. Send one or the other, not both.

NoArguments.description: This tool takes no arguments. Send `{}` or nothing at all.

BadRequest.description: Something in the request was not understood. Nothing was read.

value.message: Dates must look like 2026-04-02. Nothing was read.

Unauthorized.description: No token, the wrong token, or a token for the other door. Nothing was read. Do not retry with a different guess.

value.message: This door did not recognise the key it was given.

NotFound.description: There is no tool at that path. It is not switched off; it does not exist. Do not try a similar path.

value.message: This door has no such tool.

TooMany.description: Too many calls in the hour. Wait; do not loop.

value.message: That is as many questions as this door answers in an hour. Try again later.

Unreadable.description: The door could not read the whole ledger, so it refused to compute anything from part of it. Say exactly this and stop. Do not answer from an earlier reply, and do not estimate.

value.message: I could not read the ledger cleanly, so I am not going to give you a number.

AsOf.description: The Arizona clock this answer was computed from, as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS with no zone on the end. Arizona does not change with daylight saving. If it is present and its date is not today in Arizona, the answer is stale — say so instead of reading it out.

Money.description: US dollars, already rounded to the cent. Report it as given.

Person.description: Which of the two people. The token decides whose data may be written; for reads this says whose body log to look at.

error.description: A short code for the kind of refusal.

message.description: One plain sentence, written to be said out loud as it stands.

id.description: A stable name for the check, e.g. splits-sum.

question.description: The plain question the check asks. Prefer these words to your own.

status.description: fail means the app disagrees with itself here. It is not a maybe.

detail.description: One cleaned sentence. When a check fails it may name a bill, a budget line or a category, and it will never name a merchant or a single charge. It may end by pointing at the app.

count.description: How many things failed, when the check can count them. Absent means the count is not available — do not infer one.

broken.description: An alternative count some checks use. Treat it exactly like count.

NamedValue.description: One side of a comparison the check made. When both a and b are present, the check's job was to prove they are equal.

clean.description: True when every check passed. This is the only state worth saying nothing about.

checks.description: Every check, in the order the app runs them. The list can grow; read the ids you are given.

available.description: Spendable cash across the cash accounts. Already net of anything still processing. Do not add pending_hold to it.

pending_hold.description: How much of the recent reduction is charges still processing. Context only — it has already been taken off available.

accounts.description: One entry per cash account. Credit cards are not here; they are debts.

name.description: The household's own short name for the account, cleaned and shortened. Never a bank name and never any part of an account number.

pending_hold.description: Still processing on this account. May be absent, which means none is recorded.

debts.description: In the household's payoff order — first in the list is the one being attacked.

total.description: Everything owed, from the app's plan maths. Absent when the door cannot get it from there; in that case do not add the balances up yourself.

id.description: The app's id for this debt. Use it if you need to refer to the same debt twice; do not read it out.

name.description: The household's own name for the debt, cleaned and shortened. Any run of digits is removed, so a name may look trimmed.

apr.description: Yearly interest rate as a percent. Absent when not recorded — do not assume zero.

min_payment.description: Minimum due. Absent when not recorded.

from.description: The first day counted, echoed back. Say this date, not the words you were asked.

to.description: The last day counted, echoed back.

totals.description: Category name to dollars spent in the window. A category with no spending may be missing. These are totals only — there is no way to see the charges behind one.

PayCycle.description: The pay cycle containing right now: from the last payday through the day before the next one. It crosses the end of a month by design.

start.description: First day of the cycle, included.

end.description: Last day of the cycle, included.

label.description: The window written out, ready to say.

day.description: Which day of the cycle it is now, counting from 1.

days.description: How many days the cycle lasts.

target.description: This cycle's share of the monthly figure — not the monthly figure.

spent.description: Spent so far this cycle, including charges still processing.

label.description: The line's name as the app shows it.

target.description: This cycle's allowance for the line.

spent.description: Spent against the line this cycle.

left.description: Target minus spent. Negative means over — say over by that much.

latest.description: The most recent weigh-in in pounds. null means nothing is logged.

week_avg.description: Average of this week's weigh-ins, in pounds. Weeks start Monday. null means none this week.

week_count.description: How many days this week have a weigh-in. One day is not a week — say which it is.

lb_per_week.description: Trend in pounds per week over everything on file. Negative means losing. null means fewer than two entries, which you must say in words rather than reporting zero.
